_note: PASSIVE -- the one level that is genuinely a different plan rather than the same
plan with the dials moved (AI_Player_difficulty.md, and the project owner's own
note that this is the one that would differ a lot).
IT NEVER ATTACKS AND NEVER TRAINS A SOLDIER, so the difference is mostly what is
ABSENT: there is no barracks rule, no train-military rule and no attack rule in
this file at all. That is the point of a rule set over a flag -- 'passive' is not a
special case inside the interpreter, it is a shorter list.
TWO BELTS TO THAT BRACES, both of which matter and neither of which is redundant:
attacks: false   stops the STANDING ORDERS sending idle soldiers at the enemy.
A passive bot can still end up owning soldiers -- the map may
start it with a scout -- and without this it would throw them
at you having never decided to. This is the gate that already
existed in AISystem for AILevel.PASSIVE, moved into data.
max_age: 2       'never ages up past age 2'. Enforced in code as well as by the
absence of a second advance_age rule, so that a modder editing
this file cannot age a passive bot to 4 by adding one.
IT BUILDS DEFENCES BUT NOT TOWERS. 'never builds defense buildings (towers)' and
'can build gates and walls' read as a contradiction until you notice a tower SHOOTS
and a wall does not: passive means it will not hurt you, not that it will not shut
a door. Walls are not in the opening because nothing yet decides WHERE a wall goes
-- 5.8 built the pieces and the merge, and a bot that cannot pick a line would put
nine tiles of palisade through its own gold. Left out honestly rather than faked.
WHAT IT IS FOR: a sparring partner for testing economy and buildings without a
clock on you, and the opponent that makes an AI-vs-AI run terminate on ECONOMY
rather than on a rush -- which is the harder half of the balance question.
